main_text.p: furum, & infert malum actuale: scilicet hoc est satisfacere Deum luæ[?] bonitati & amori. 7. At quæro cui bonitati satisfacit Deus, bonitati in creaturas collatæ? An naturali bonitati Dei ad intra? Si prius, nec adhuc satisfactu tali bonitati: nam nihil boni reprobis confertur, quin imo miseriæ gravissimæ hoc bono implicantur. Si posterius, non satisfieri omnino potest bo-nitati Dei naturali ad intra, quippe cum ni-hil additur, nihil adimitur, cui nec feritur, nec metitur, etiamsi nullos mortales voca-ret ad beatitudinem. 8. In voce (præcisè) Corvinus præcisum impostorem agit. Non enim per (præcisè) intelligit intense & ve-hementer: cur enim Dei desideria circa o-bedientiam, & salutem reproborum, sint minus remissa, quam ipsius desideria circa obedientiam & salutem electorum? In Dei præ如destinatione, nolunt causam quæri: at alibi esse non potest; si per (præcisè) in-telligit absolute, tum Dei intentio circa o-bedientiam & salutem reproborum est condi-tionalis: at qua conditione intendit ut re-probi obediant? Ex hypothesi, quod velint, hoc est, ex hypothesi quod obediant. En quas dictitat nugas? At vero si Pharisæi re-jecerunt Dei consilium conditionatum, id-tam ponit Pharisæos non obedituros, quam obedituros, & sic non est spretum. Imo si Deus intendit damnare Pharisæos, si non obedierint, tam non obediendo, quam obe-diendo, spernunt Dei consilium: quo quid abfur-

page.notes: Page number "183" is set in a form with a yogh-like final digit; read as 183 with a doubt marked. Running head is in small capitals and ends in an exclamation mark, copied as printed. Two words are doubtful: "luæ" (possibly "luæ" for lux, set in the old form) and "præ如destinatione" which contains a stray character; the intended word is "prædestinatione", and it is marked as printed in the scan. The word "idtam" at the line end is printed with a dot or hyphen and is joined here; the separation may be "id-tam". The text ends mid-word on "abfur-" with no catchword. Long s is written as plain s throughout, including in "desideria" and "remissa", where the scan shows a long-s form.
